children: Gold futures fell as U.S. payrolls increased well above expectations in August, pushing up short-term Treasury yields and raising expectations of a possible September Fed hike. President Trump, however, called for lower interest rates following the employment report. "A resilient labor market would give the Fed permission to move rates higher at the September meeting if upcoming August inflation data does not show continued improvement, but that political pressure to maintain lower rates looms in the background," Mike Castle of StoneX says in a note. Front month gold settles down 1.4% at $4,429.80 a troy ounce for a 1.1% loss on the week. Silver falls 1.4% to $66.047, also a 1.4% weekly loss. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
